description: Jinny Lee is a dedicated real estate professional in East Auckland, helping homeowners achieve premium results and guiding buyers to secure the right property with confidence. Backed by Ray White Botany, Jinny combines strong local knowledge, strategic marketing, and a client-first approach.
tone: warm yet confident, trustworthy, knowledgeable, approachable, community-focused, client-first

brand_positioning.jinny_role: trusted East Auckland real estate advisor
brand_positioning.differentiation: local market expertise, strong negotiation skills, personalised service

target_audience.secondary: buyers and families searching for homes in East Auckland
target_audience.entry_level: first-home buyers needing guidance and education

optimal_times: 08:00 — highest single-post engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 3, image post, April 19); confirmed as a top-performing hour in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for morning-scroll educational content and listing reveals targeting commuters and early risers in East Auckland; image posts at this hour produced the strongest available engagement signal in the data period and should be prioritised for seller education and listing content; this window was never used across all 9 archived local posts which defaulted uniformly to 20:00 — correcting this omission is an immediate scheduling priority

10:00 — second-highest engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 2, image post, April 13); confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for mid-morning market update and buyer guidance content when the East Auckland audience is actively browsing on mobile; image format confirmed as the top format at this hour; also absent from all 9 archived local posts — introducing mid-morning scheduling alongside morning posts will diversify reach across different audience browsing patterns

21:00 — confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and appearing in top-5 Facebook insight posts with engagement score of 1; closely aligned with the consistent 20:00 posting pattern across all 9 archived local posts; recommended as the primary evening window targeting homeowners in a relaxed end-of-day planning mindset; best suited for seller education, community content, and interest rate commentary when audiences are in a reflective decision-making state

20:00 — most common posting hour across all 9 archived local posts; retained as a secondary evening fallback window closely aligned with the 21:00 insights peak; use when 21:00 scheduling is unavailable or when content is time-sensitive on a given day; avoid making this the only posting window as the previous strategy did across both consecutive periods — split scheduling across morning and evening windows is now the recommended approach to maximise daily reach
best_days: Tuesday through Thursday recommended as primary posting days for seller education, market update, and buyer guidance content based on general real estate social media best practices — low confidence due to insufficient day-level performance data in the current Facebook insights period; reassess when day-level engagement data becomes available in the next 30-day review cycle

Saturday morning at 08:00 to 10:00 recommended for listing reveals, open home announcements, and sold result posts to align with weekend buyer browsing and open home activity patterns in East Auckland — supported by 08:00 and 10:00 confirmed as top-performing hours in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and general real estate audience behaviour on weekends

Sunday evening at 20:00 to 21:00 recommended for seller education and week-ahead market content targeting East Auckland homeowners in a relaxed end-of-weekend planning mindset — supported by the 21:00 performance signal from Facebook insights and the consistent 20:00 archive posting pattern; autumn urgency and interest rate hooks are the recommended content themes for this slot
learned.image_to_text_ratio: 3:1 — minimum three image or video posts for every one text-only post per week; the current archive is 0:9 in favour of text which is the inverse of recommended best practice per brand identity visual guidelines and all five research briefs across two consecutive strategy periods; the two highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period were both image posts confirming visual formats outperform text even in a low-data environment; this ratio shift is the most urgent and overdue tactical change required and must be implemented and maintained from the current week forward without exception
top_content_types: listing — hero interior and exterior shots showcasing lifestyle, indoor-outdoor flow, and premium East Auckland homes; confirmed as primary format based on brand identity guidelines and the two highest-engagement Facebook posts both being image posts at 08:00 and 10:00; low confidence due to zero reach and impression data in current period; must be published at confirmed peak hours of 08:00 or 10:00 to replicate the conditions of the top-performing posts; this format remains entirely absent from the 9-post archive across two consecutive strategy periods and must be introduced immediately

lifestyle — family living moments, warm autumn-toned interiors, soft natural light through windows, indoor-outdoor connection; seasonal alignment with Autumn 2026 context confirmed across all five research briefs; autumn lifestyle framing is the dominant seasonal content opportunity cited this period and should be the visual tone applied across all image post types through end of April into early May before winter market slowdown begins in June

sold — celebration moments, sold sticker overlays, happy client handovers at front door with genuine emotion; social proof format cited across three separate research briefs as a direct trust-building driver of seller enquiries; entirely absent from the current 9-post archive across two consecutive strategy periods making it the single highest-priority image type to introduce immediately; at least one sold story image post per week is recommended as a non-negotiable content element

local_area — East Auckland streets, parks, school zones, suburban greenery, tree-lined streets, coastal lifestyle shots; suburb spotlight and school zone content noted across multiple research briefs as consistently building local authority and trust with family buyer audiences; currently absent from the archive and underrepresented relative to recommended content pillar weighting; aligns with autumn school-term family research cycle making it timely and high-relevance right now; multigenerational living demand flagged as a medium-relevance emerging trend across two briefs and East Auckland housing stock makes this a natural local authority angle to introduce this period

agent_brand — Jinny interacting with clients at open homes, behind-the-scenes of listing process, professional yet warm and approachable moments; transparency and personal brand content cited in the April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions; absent from the current archive across two consecutive periods and recommended for introduction to close the social proof and personality content gap; behind-the-scenes listing process walkthrough format specifically cited in two research briefs as building the trust needed to convert seller enquiries during active market conditions
top_pillars: Seller Education — autumn selling season is at peak relevance across all five research briefs generated between April 15 and April 23; education posts on pricing strategy, home staging, listing preparation, pre-winter timing, and the cost of waiting are consistently cited as high-engagement save-and-share formats; this pillar should lead the weekly content mix at 30 percent weighting through the end of April and into early May while seasonal urgency is at its highest point before the winter market slowdown arrives in June; interest rate cut angles must be woven into seller education content this period as they are flagged as high-relevance across all five briefs

Trends and Short-form Content — short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format in April 2026 across multiple research briefs; introducing at least one TikTok or Instagram Reel per week is the single highest-priority format gap to close given the current text-only archive across two consecutive strategy periods; behind-the-scenes listing process content, open home walkthroughs, quick property tip videos, and one-thing-sellers-forget formats are the recommended entry formats for this pillar; this format has never appeared in the archive and algorithm momentum on video-first platforms depends on consistency starting now

Personal Brand and Trust — behind-the-scenes listing process content and transparency posts cited in the April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions; sold celebration stories and client handover moments are entirely absent from the current 9-post archive across two consecutive strategy periods and must be introduced immediately as a weekly priority to build social proof with potential sellers who are evaluating agents during the active autumn season; Jinny's personal brand presence in content is a direct differentiator from generic agent content and must be visible at least once per week

Listings and Success Stories — sold results and client success case studies cited across three of five research briefs as social proof drivers of seller enquiries; this format is entirely absent from the current archive across two consecutive strategy periods and represents the most significant missed trust-conversion opportunity; at least one sold story or case study post per week is recommended immediately and should be maintained as a non-negotiable weekly content element until a visible social proof pattern is established on the profile
